chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, who said:

Indeed, Allah the Exalted permitted the private parts based on the capacity of the servants regarding strength in paying the dower and ability to keep (them), so He said: 'Marry such women as seem good to you, two and three and four; but if you fear that you will not do justice (between them), then (marry) only one or what your right hands possess'; and He said: 'And whoever among you has not within his power ampleness of means to marry free believing women, then (he may marry) of those whom your right hands possess from among your believing maidens'; and He said: 'Then as to those whom you enjoy with, give them their dowries as appointed; and there is no blame on you about what you mutually agree after what is appointed'.

Thus, Allah permitted the private parts for the people of strength according to their strength in giving the dower and ability to keep: four for the one who is able to do that; and for the one below that, three, two, and one; and the one who is not able to keep one should marry the possession of the right hand. And when he is not able to keep her, nor able to marry the free woman, nor able to buy the slave girl, then Allah has permitted temporary marriage with the easiest of what he can manage from the dower, and without the necessity of expenses.

And Allah made self-sufficient each group from them with whatever He gave them of strength in giving the dower and ability in expenses regarding keeping, and regarding keeping regarding chastity from immorality; otherwise they would be given from Allah Mighty and Majestic good assistance, and given strength, and pointed towards the permissible aspect due to what He gave them that would make them chaste from the prohibited in what He gave them and made them needless from the prohibited, and clarified that for them.

Thus, at that time, He placed the legal punishments upon them, from whipping, stoning, cursing, and separation; and had Allah not made self-sufficient each group from them with what He made for them the way to the permissible aspects, He would not have placed a legal punishment from these legal punishments upon them.

So, as for the aspect of permanent marriage and the aspect of possession of the right hand, its proof is clear and obvious in the hands of the people due to the frequency of their dealing with it between themselves. And as for the matter of temporary marriage, it is an ambiguous matter upon many due to the reason of the forbidding of the one who forbade from it and prohibited it, even though it existed in the Revelation and was transmitted in the comprehensive Sunnah for the one who seeks its reason and intends that.

Therefore, temporary marriage became permissible for the rich and the poor, so they would be equal in the permissibility of the private parts, just as they were equal in fulfilling the rituals of Hajj, the temporary marriage of Hajj, thus whatever is easier from the sacrifice for the rich and the poor. Thus, the rich entered into this interpretation due to the reason of the poor ones, and that is that the obligations were placed upon the lowest of the people in strength, to accommodate the rich and the poor; and that is because it is not allowed that obligations be imposed according to the capacities of the people, so the strength of the strong cannot be distinguished from the weakness of the weak, but they were placed based on the strength of the weakest of the weak.

Then the strong ones were urged, so they rushed in goodness with the optional acts due to the surplus of strength in themselves and wealth. And temporary marriage is permissible for the rich and the poor, for the people of ability, from the one who has four and from the one who has possession of the right hand, as much as he wishes, just as it is permissible for the one who finds nothing except the strength for the dower of temporary marriage. And the dower is whatever they mutually agree upon within the limits of marriage, for the rich and the poor, little or much.

key_terms.مِلْكُ الْيَمِينِ: Possession of the right hand (slave girl)

ai.seo_question: What is the theological and legal justification for temporary marriage (Mut'ah) in Shia Islam according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential rationale for the hierarchy of marital permissions, positing that divine laws are calibrated to the capacity of the weakest individual to ensure universal applicability. It specifically highlights Mut'ah (temporary marriage) as a flexible, egalitarian solution for both the rich and poor to preserve chastity, with its dower determined by mutual consent rather than fixed obligations. This perspective underscores the Shia view of Mut'ah as a distinct, permanent institution often obscured by later Sunni interpretations that emphasized its abrogation.
